nodes.label: Available Departments
nodes.rationale: Departments are predefined as HR, Accounting, Admin, Maintenance, MIS, Teacher. No foreign key since values are fixed.

nodes.label: 5-Stage Approval Workflow
nodes.rationale: Uses 5-stage workflow: Noted, Checked, Verified, Issued, Approved. Each stage records who performed the action and when via dedicated columns on supply_request table.

nodes.label: Socratic Gate
nodes.rationale: The Socratic Gate ensures that even when users provide detailed requirements, edge cases and trade-offs are still considered before implementation begins, preventing assumptions-driven development.

nodes.label: Intelligent Agent Routing
nodes.rationale: Before responding to any request, the system automatically analyzes the request domain and selects the most appropriate specialist agent, maintaining silent analysis without verbose commentary.

nodes.label: Request Classifier
nodes.rationale: Requests are classified into QUESTION, SURVEY, SIMPLE CODE, COMPLEX CODE, DESIGN, or SLASH CMD types, each triggering a different agent and execution workflow.

nodes.label: Testing Pyramid
nodes.rationale: Testing should follow a pyramid structure with many unit tests, some integration tests, and few E2E tests for efficient coverage.

nodes.label: Page Object Model (POM)
nodes.rationale: Test files should never query selectors directly; all selectors should be abstracted into Page Classes for maintainability.

nodes.label: Zero Trust Architecture
nodes.rationale: Never trust, always verify. Assume breach, design as if attacker is already inside, enforce least privilege and defense in depth.

nodes.label: E-E-A-T Framework
nodes.rationale: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness - four pillars for demonstrating content quality to both traditional and AI-powered search engines.

nodes.label: SEO and GEO Dual Targeting
nodes.rationale: Content must simultaneously target traditional search engines (SEO via keywords, backlinks) and AI-powered search engines (GEO via entities, data, credentials, citations).

nodes.label: Four-Phase Workflow (BMAD)
nodes.rationale: ANALYSIS (research) -> PLANNING ({task-slug}.md creation) -> SOLUTIONING (architecture, no code) -> IMPLEMENTATION (code + tests) -> VERIFICATION. No code is written before Phase 4.

nodes.label: Project Type Detection
nodes.rationale: Projects are classified as WEB, MOBILE, or BACKEND type, each selecting a different primary agent. Mobile projects exclusively use mobile-developer, never frontend-specialist.

nodes.label: MoSCoW and RICE Prioritization
nodes.rationale: MoSCoW (Must/Should/Could/Won't) and RICE (Reach/Impact/Confidence/Effort) frameworks for backlog prioritization and trade-off evaluation.

nodes.label: REST API Style
nodes.rationale: REST is best for public APIs with widest compatibility across platforms and consumers. Uses nouns for resources, HTTP methods for actions, and standard status codes.

nodes.label: GraphQL API Style
nodes.rationale: GraphQL is best for complex, interconnected data needs with multiple frontend platforms requiring flexible queries. Solves over-fetching and under-fetching.

nodes.label: tRPC API Style
nodes.rationale: tRPC is best for TypeScript monorepos where end-to-end type safety with zero schema maintenance and automatic type inference is critical.

nodes.label: JWT Authentication
nodes.rationale: JWT is best for stateless authentication in microservices. Always verify signature, check expiration, use short expiry with refresh tokens, never store sensitive data in JWT.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0 Authentication
nodes.rationale: OAuth 2.0 is best for third-party integration scenarios where delegated authorization is required.

nodes.label: Envelope Response Pattern
nodes.rationale: Consistent response format using { success, data, error } envelope for predictable API consumption.

nodes.label: Cursor-based Pagination
nodes.rationale: Cursor pagination is best for large frequently-changing datasets where offset pagination would cause performance issues or inconsistent results.

nodes.label: URI-based Versioning
nodes.rationale: URI versioning (/v1/users) is preferred for public APIs because it provides clear, easy-to-cache separation between API versions.

nodes.label: Token Bucket Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Token bucket is the recommended rate limiting strategy for most APIs as it allows burst traffic while enforcing average limits over time.

nodes.label: App Builder Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: The App Builder orchestrator analyzes user requests, determines tech stack, plans structure, and coordinates specialist agents through a defined pipeline.

nodes.label: Agent Coordination Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The pipeline flows: App Builder -> Project Planner (PLAN.md) -> Plan Verification Checkpoint -> Database Architect/Backend/Frontend Specialists -> Parallel Security + Test -> DevOps Engineer.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure for Skills
nodes.rationale: Skills remain in inactive state until triggered by matching request description, avoiding tool bloat and reducing context window usage by only loading relevant specialized knowledge.

nodes.label: BOLA/IDOR Vulnerability (OWASP API1)
nodes.rationale: Broken Object Level Authorization is the top OWASP API security risk. Testing involves identifying resource IDs in requests and replaying with another user's session to verify access control.

nodes.label: Plan Verification Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Phase 1.5 is a mandatory checkpoint between project planning and specialist agent execution. No specialist agent proceeds without PLAN.md file verification.
